# OCR: scanned CVs through the NLP pipeline (generated by `python -m app.eval.ocr`; do not edit by hand)

30 clean CVs of the `coding` set (half English, half Vietnamese) rendered as image-only PDFs and read back through `read_file` → PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5 (`lang="vi"`, the latin model) → `process`. Gold: the generator's latent facts. *text (no OCR)* is the same CVs read as text: the difference is the cost of OCR.

| Condition | slice | CER | tool P / R / F1 | years within 1 y | experience section found | s / page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| text (no OCR) | all | 0.000 | 0.995 / 1.000 / 0.997 | 27/30 | 30/30 | — |
|  | en | 0.000 | 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 | 15/15 | 15/15 | — |
|  | vi | 0.000 | 0.989 / 1.000 / 0.995 | 12/15 | 15/15 | — |
| scan | all | 0.031 | 0.995 / 1.000 / 0.997 | 27/30 | 30/30 | 9.1 |
|  | en | 0.003 | 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 | 15/15 | 15/15 | 9.8 |
|  | vi | 0.060 | 0.989 / 1.000 / 0.995 | 12/15 | 15/15 | 8.4 |
| phone photo | all | 0.036 | 0.995 / 1.000 / 0.997 | 27/30 | 30/30 | 8.8 |
|  | en | 0.009 | 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 | 15/15 | 15/15 | 9.4 |
|  | vi | 0.063 | 0.989 / 1.000 / 0.995 | 12/15 | 15/15 | 8.2 |

## Before → after the three fixes

The first run found three defects, all in how our pipeline reads OCR output, none in the benchmark data:
capital I read as "l" in tool names (`ocr.fix_capital_i`), Vietnamese headings with dropped letters (`segment.loose_heading`) and PII labels with dropped letters (`redact.loose_kind`). Same OCR text, re-scored:

| Condition | tool recall | Vietnamese CVs with an experience section | Vietnamese address leaks | Vietnamese gender leaks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| scan | 0.925 → 1.000 | 0/15 → 15/15 | 15/15 → 0/15 | 6/15 → 0/15 |
| phone photo | 0.935 → 1.000 | 0/15 → 15/15 | 15/15 → 0/15 | 6/15 → 0/15 |

What the latin model reads on a Vietnamese scan (syn_181, first 160 characters):

```
Nguyn Văn Hùng
Automation Test Engineer
```
